CAP-ATTACH-SPECIES-ROLE.activation: For any possible agent, write SELF first: what change does that reactant itself undergo?
CAP-ATTACH-SPECIES-ROLE.familiar_macro_anchor: Use a fresh symbolic reaction to prove a reactant role from equation evidence. The role name comes after the self-change, not before it.
CAP-ATTACH-SPECIES-ROLE.learner_title: Prove the species role from its own change
CAP-ATTACH-SPECIES-ROLE.ordinary_language_explanation: An oxidising or reducing agent is named from the change it undergoes and causes. Prove the self-change first.
reconstruction_steps: Track the reactant itself.
State whether its oxidation state rises or falls.
State the corresponding effect on the other reactant.
Attach the agent role only after those two statements agree.
CAP-ATTACH-SPECIES-ROLE.rule_model_condition: SELF change is evidence; the agent label is the conclusion. Never reverse that order.
CAP-ATTACH-SPECIES-ROLE.transfer_bridge: Agent vocabulary is a Redox depth extension and is not attributed to the eleven retained NCERT source asks.

CAP-CLASSIFY-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.activation: Before naming the change, underline the evidence that tells you whether a new substance appears.
CAP-CLASSIFY-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.familiar_macro_anchor: Rusting, burning, heating and gas evolution can look dramatic, but the deciding question is whether the evidence supports formation of a new substance.
CAP-CLASSIFY-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.learner_title: Decide whether the evidence shows a chemical change
CAP-CLASSIFY-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.misconception_contrast: Two questions may both mention heating: one can be only a state change, while another forms new substances. Heating itself is not the classifier.
CAP-CLASSIFY-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.ordinary_language_explanation: Do not classify from a familiar word alone. Read the stated evidence first, decide what changed, and only then name the change or property.
reconstruction_steps: Write the observation or process that is actually stated.
Ask whether the evidence shows a new substance or chemical reaction.
Classify only after that evidence test.
Check that the reason and the class agree.
CAP-CLASSIFY-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.rule_model_condition: A physical change does not create a new substance; a chemical change does. Use only the evidence supplied in the question.
CAP-CLASSIFY-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.transfer_bridge: Use the same evidence-first routine on every retained NCERT classification item before moving to explicit Redox bookkeeping.

CAP-SEPARATE-OBSERVATION-INFERENCE.activation: Make two columns: what you actually observe or test, and what you infer from it.
CAP-SEPARATE-OBSERVATION-INFERENCE.familiar_macro_anchor: A smell, a pop test or gas evolution is evidence. The name of the gas is the inference supported by that evidence.
CAP-SEPARATE-OBSERVATION-INFERENCE.learner_title: Keep the observation separate from the chemical inference
CAP-SEPARATE-OBSERVATION-INFERENCE.misconception_contrast: ‘A gas is evolved’ is an observation; ‘the gas is hydrogen’ is an inference that needs a supporting test.
CAP-SEPARATE-OBSERVATION-INFERENCE.ordinary_language_explanation: Write the observation first. Then state the chemical claim it supports. This prevents a remembered answer from being written as though it were an observation.
reconstruction_steps: Copy the observation or test result without interpreting it.
Write the possible chemical inference separately.
Link the evidence to the inference.
Check that the inference is no stronger than the evidence.
CAP-SEPARATE-OBSERVATION-INFERENCE.rule_model_condition: The claim must not say more than the recorded observation or test can support.
CAP-SEPARATE-OBSERVATION-INFERENCE.transfer_bridge: Use this evidence-to-claim route on the iron–sulphur gas-identification source question and on later reaction evidence.

CAP-TRACK-OXIDATION-STATE.activation: Write the oxidation state of the same element before and after the reaction on one horizontal lane.
CAP-TRACK-OXIDATION-STATE.familiar_macro_anchor: After the NCERT source-practice denominator is protected, use a fresh Zn/Cu²⁺ reaction to make the numerical Redox bookkeeping explicit.
CAP-TRACK-OXIDATION-STATE.learner_title: Use an oxidation-state lane to prove oxidation and reduction
CAP-TRACK-OXIDATION-STATE.ordinary_language_explanation: Oxidation is an increase in oxidation state; reduction is a decrease. Track the same element before comparing the numbers.
reconstruction_steps: Write the before oxidation state for the element.
Write the after oxidation state for the same element.
Compare the two values and state increase or decrease.
Name oxidation only for an increase and reduction only for a decrease.
CAP-TRACK-OXIDATION-STATE.rule_model_condition: In Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, Zn changes from oxidation state 0 to +2 and Cu changes from +2 to 0. Track oxidation state as a bookkeeping value for the same element; do not confuse the idea with a claim about isolated particles in every compound.
CAP-TRACK-OXIDATION-STATE.transfer_bridge: Use the lane as a proof tool on fresh Redox reactions after the NCERT source-practice denominator is closed.

CAP-TRACK-REACTING-SPECIES.activation: Write the reaction as a before/after map and point to the same element on both sides.
CAP-TRACK-REACTING-SPECIES.familiar_macro_anchor: After the NCERT source-practice ideas about chemical change are secure, use a separate fresh symbolic reaction to learn Redox tracking without giving away any retained source answer.
CAP-TRACK-REACTING-SPECIES.learner_title: Track the same reacting species before naming Redox change
CAP-TRACK-REACTING-SPECIES.ordinary_language_explanation: A Redox label is earned by tracking what happens to the same element or species across the reaction.
reconstruction_steps: Identify the reactant species.
Locate the same elements in the product.
Mark what changes and what is preserved.
Only then move to oxidation-state or agent labels.
CAP-TRACK-REACTING-SPECIES.rule_model_condition: Track identity first; do not assign oxidation, reduction or agent roles from reagent reputation.
CAP-TRACK-REACTING-SPECIES.transfer_bridge: This is a Redox depth extension using a fresh reaction; it is not an extra NCERT source question and does not reveal a retained source answer.

marking_points: Identify rusting as corrosion.
State that it is a chemical change.
Select melting, bending and drawing into wire as physical changes.
Exclude rusting because it is a chemical change.
State that strong heating causes iron and sulphur to react.
State that a new substance, iron sulphide, is formed.
Classify the statement as a chemical property.
Use reaction with hydrochloric acid and hydrogen-gas evolution as the evidence.
Identify rusting as corrosion.
State that rusting is a chemical change because a new substance forms.
Classify the decomposition as a chemical change.
Use formation of calcium oxide and carbon dioxide as evidence of new substances.
Name oxygen as the required non-metal for combustion.
For heated part A, identify hydrogen sulphide; it has a foul smell and turns lead acetate solution black.
For unheated part B, identify hydrogen; it burns with a pop sound.
Classify burning of kerosene as a chemical change.
State that combustion forms new substances.
Select melting, bending and drawing into wire as physical changes.
Exclude rusting because it forms a new substance.
Select decaying and burning of wood as chemical changes.
Do not classify sawing or hammering as chemical changes.

scope_statement: The eleven retained NCERT items are the governed source-practice denominator. Oxidation-state and agent-role teaching is a clearly separated Redox depth extension derived from reaction evidence; it is not presented as additional NCERT source questions.

PF-EVIDENCE_TO_CLAIM.h1: Write only what is observed or tested before naming the substance or product.
PF-EVIDENCE_TO_CLAIM.h2: Keep evidence and inference in separate lines; the inference must be supported by the observation or test.
PF-EVIDENCE_TO_CLAIM.h3: Draw two columns headed ‘observation/test’ and ‘inference’, then fill the left column first.

PF-REACTION_PROCESS_CLASSIFICATION.h1: Underline the word, observation or product that actually decides the answer.
PF-REACTION_PROCESS_CLASSIFICATION.h2: Use the evidence test: a chemical change forms new substance(s); a physical change does not. For a named reaction requirement, use the process definition stated in the lesson.
PF-REACTION_PROCESS_CLASSIFICATION.h3: Write ‘new substance or reaction evidence?’ and answer that line before you classify or choose.
